Quick sizing sketch and tradeoffs (high level):

Summary recommendation:
- Baseline Dedicated pool: 4x H100-class GPUs for the low-latency interactive path + 6x A40/A10-equivalent GPUs to soak batch throughput and handle weekend bursts. Set autoscale/burst policy to add 4 additional A10s for the highest short-term spikes. This gives predictable p95 latency for interactive and cost-effective throughput for batch.

Rationale and assumptions:
- Model: assume single LLM variant with 500 tokens total per call and medium decoding complexity. If you run >1 heavy model concurrently, add headroom.
- H100-class for interactive: lower latency and higher single-request throughput for long context/kv-cache sensitive calls. We size 4 H100s assuming each can sustain ~30–40 steady TPS at ~200–250ms p95 for 500-token calls under continuous load (depends on model specifics). That maps to ~120–160 interactive TPS headroom.
- A10/A40 fleet for batch: cheaper per-GPU throughput; each A10-equivalent can handle ~80–120 TPS when serving batched requests. 6 A10s = ~480–720 TPS baseline; autoscale + burst will cover weekends.
- Autoscale policy: keep reserved pool (4 H100 + 6 A10) and allow burst add of 4 A10s when queue depth or 95th latency exceeds threshold.

Quantization & model variants:
- If you can use an 8-bit quantized variant for batch-only jobs, throughput per cheaper GPU improves ~1.5–2x and cost drops. Keep full-precision or 16-bit variant on H100s for interactive to preserve quality/latency.

Private vs Dedicated callouts:
- If BlueHarbor requires customer-managed KMS/HSM or full air-gapped on-prem, steer to Private. VPC peering + SOC2 + encrypted logs typically allow Dedicated with VPC control plane.

Next steps for proposal:
- I can produce an ops-level runbook and a 30/60/90 POC config with expected token-based cost estimates if they confirm the workbook numbers. Ben — can you draft a matching pricing ballpark we can attach?

—Karthik
